result_basis: Both lanes were correct on the same fixture and succeeded without retries. Both touched one implementation file and required no lane-specific human message. Conventional automation required 10 changed lines in code versus 12 changed lines in compositional configuration. The compositional lane preserved engine code unchanged, which is a real locality/modularity property, but this challenge did not demonstrate lower measured adaptation burden.
original_interpretation: CCS-016 does not support the hypothesis that the compositional architecture reduces adaptation burden for this policy change. Its config-only adaptation may matter under repeated or larger changes, but that value was not established here and should be tested rather than assumed.

external_review.locality_observation: The compositional lane changed configuration while the conventional lane changed code; this is an observed separation-of-policy property, not a demonstrated scale or cost advantage.
